transcript:
Date: 2026-11-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Ravi Malhotra (CTO - Canyon Edge), Sophie Lane (Head of Platform), Ethan Wu (Security Engineer)

Summary: quick discovery focused on private/VPC deployment requirements, region constraints, peering and private endpoints; discussed security posture and next steps to run a small pilot and network validation

00:00 - 00:18 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, i'm maya from redwood, with liam our se, we wanted to learn about canyon edge's infra and what success looks like for a private deployment
00:19 - 00:42 Ravi: thanks maya, yeah we run a customer support LLM and some insights pipelines, latency sensitive on some endpoints, compliance needs, and we are evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs fully private vpc deployment
00:43 - 01:15 Liam: great, can you walk me through current cloud region, vpc setup, and any hard constraints around cross-region traffic or peering? also curious about your security requirements like kms and sso
01:16 - 01:38 Sophie: we're on AWS primarily, account in us-west-2, and we have a strict policy that traffic must not egress to public internet for inference; we prefer private endpoints or vpc peering. we also have a eu region presence but want to keep inference in us-west-2 for now
01:39 - 02:10 Ethan: security side, we need SOC2 type II, audit logs, and key management with our KMS; HSM would be a plus. also SAML SSO for console access and RBAC for ops roles
02:11 - 02:35 Maya: that's common, Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC with private endpoint and peering, we can integrate with your KMS and support SSO via SAML; will confirm HSM options with infra
02:36 - 03:05 Liam: to add, our runtime can be deployed in your subnet, we typically recommend a dedicated subnet for inference with egress control. we do have some docs on VPC peering vs PrivateLink style private endpoint — peering is simpler but PrivateLink avoids cross-account route table changes
03:06 - 03:45 Ravi: curious about latency tradeoffs. if we run Private in us-west-2 vs Redwood hosted, what's the expected token latency difference? and costs? we want consistent p95 under 200ms for critical chat flows
03:46 - 04:25 Liam: right, p95 depends on model size and batch settings; a private, on-premises/private VPC setup avoids public networking hops and typically matches hosted latency ±10-20ms, but costs differ — dedicated or private has fixed infra plus run costs; we can share examples. caching (prefix/KV cache) helps a lot for repetitive prompts
04:26 - 05:00 Sophie: okay and what about autoscaling — we might have bursty loads when product launches happen. can private deployment autoscale across more GPUs or burst to Redwood dedicated capacity?
05:01 - 05:40 Maya: yes, we have options: Dedicated pools with reserved capacity and burst to hosted is a typical pattern; for private we can do hybrid routing: primary to your private cluster with failover to Redwood-hosted model variants in case of capacity issues, subject to policy and data controls
05:41 - 06:12 Ethan: data residency question: even if we burst to hosted, does that mean customer data leaves our vpc? we need it to remain encrypted and not be stored beyond inference window
06:13 - 06:50 Liam: good question — our routing policy can be configured to never route PII-sensitive routes to hosted; for general fallbacks we can use scrubbers or model variants. we'll document retention, and by default logs are forwarded to your audit storage; we can also ensure no persistent storage of payloads in the hosted fallback if required
06:51 - 07:20 Ravi: on networking, our network team is picky: they want to see a diagram, required security groups, peering CIDR, endpoints and route table changes. can you provide that?
07:21 - 07:45 Maya: yes, we'll send a network diagram and a VPC peering checklist. Liam will include required SG ports (e.g., 443 in/out to internal endpoints), healthcheck ports, and subnets sizes
07:46 - 08:22 Sophie: region constraints — we have EU customers later but first rollout in US-west-2; we may want EU region later, will Redwood support cross-region private deployments and data residency?
08:23 - 09:05 Liam: we support private deployment in multiple regions; cross-region requirements mean separate private clusters per region; we can replicate models and have region-aware routing. for data residency we'd recommend separate clusters in-region for EU data flows
09:06 - 09:48 Ravi: one concern: firewall and egress rules — our infra team enforces strict egress only via proxy and with TLS inspection; will Redwood Private require outbound internet to pull model updates or container images?
09:49 - 10:30 Liam: images can be pushed through a controlled pipeline. for full air-gapped setups we support customer-managed registries or pre-staged images. for typical VPC deployment, minimal outbound to Redwood control plane can be locked to specific IPs or endpoints; we'll document that precisely
10:31 - 11:10 Ethan: about encryption keys — we want KMS integration with our key rotation policy. can Redwood use our KMS for data at rest and for model key material?
11:11 - 11:45 Maya: yes, Redwood Private can integrate with your KMS for secrets and encryption; HSM availability is an enterprise feature — we'll confirm exact support and any extra compliance docs needed
11:46 - 12:30 Ravi: compliance — send us SOC2 docs and any penetration test reports you can share. also how you handle audit logging and log retention window
12:31 - 13:05 Maya: we'll include SOC2/ISO summaries, audit log architecture, and configurable retention options. we can also sign a data processing addendum and do a security review with your team
13:06 - 13:58 Sophie: operationally, how do rollouts work? can we pin model versions and do canary deploys within the private cluster? we need predictable rollbacks if quality regresses
13:59 - 14:40 Liam: yes, Redwood supports version pinning, canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. the console shows per-route metrics and we can tie evals/qa suites to trigger alerts on regressions
14:41 - 15:18 Ravi: benchmarking — we want you to run a bench with our 10k sample prompts and measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens for both hosted and private. can you do that quickly?
15:19 - 16:00 Liam: yes we'll run a short bench on a 2-node private sim and compare against hosted; findings usually surface tradeoffs with quantized models, and batching config. i'll include recommended quantization profiles and batching params to hit latency targets
16:01 - 16:45 Sophie: pricing — we need a ballpark for dedicated monthly reserved capacity vs private deployment capex/opex; also any minimum commitments
16:46 - 17:20 Maya: we'll provide ballpark numbers; dedicated has monthly commit tiers, private has an enterprise licensing model plus infra. we'll propose a pilot pricing for the first 3 months to validate
17:21 - 18:10 Ethan: network test — we might want to run a connectivity test before any provisioning; is there a peering test flow or checklist?
18:11 - 18:52 Liam: yes, we have a peering validation checklist and a small agent you can run to test connectivity and cert exchange; we'll share that in the network pack
18:53 - 19:30 Ravi: what's the expected lead time to get a private cluster into our vpc? and who manages updates?
19:31 - 20:10 Maya: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for pilot (network validation, infra setup, model onboarding), full production depends on sizing and governance; updates can be managed by Redwood or your infra team depending on arrangement
20:11 - 21:00 Sophie: support SLAs and alerting — we want 24/7 incident support for production and runbooks for failover to hosted if needed
21:01 - 21:45 Maya: enterprise support add-on covers 24/7 pager; runbooks and playbooks are provided and integrated into the Console's alerting; we'll include that in the proposal
21:46 - 22:30 Ethan: any blockers we should be aware of? e.g., VPC CIDR conflicts, cross-account role permissions?
22:31 - 23:05 Liam: main blockers are route table overlap and strict egress restrictions; cross-account IAM roles are straightforward but require your security team's sign-off ahead of provisioning
23:06 - 24:00 Ravi: ok sounds good. next steps and recap?
24:01 - 24:40 Maya: recap — we'll send network diagram, VPC peering checklist, SOC2/security pack, and a proposal with pilot pricing. liam will run the bench with your sample prompts and ethan will share the CIDRs and network constraints. schedule follow-up deep-dive with your network team week of 11/30
24:41 - 25:15 Sophie: thanks, please include the specific ports and healthcheck endpoints in the doc, and note the private endpoint vs peering pros/cons
25:16 - 25:50 Maya: will do, and i'll include a note on hybrid routing and policy to prevent sensitive routes from leaving your vpc
25:51 - 26:30 Ravi: last Q — if we start pilot and find model quality mismatch, can we iterate on quantization and caching without a big infra change?
26:31 - 27:10 Liam: yes, most perf/quality tuning is at model and runtime config level: quantization profiles, KV cache sizes, batch tuning. infra changes aren't required for those experiments
27:11 - 27:55 Maya: great, any other questions from the team?
27:56 - 28:20 Ethan: none for now, thanks
28:21 - 28:50 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and schedule.
